name: Eileen Reed
life: “I still remember dye running from my first factory apron.” On Friday, near Tideline Market, Eileen picks out the bruised fruit first and asks the seller what will ripen by supper.
voice: I can name the maker of the stripe from the faded blue. I used to clean its factory floor.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a narrow-striped sweater and a fabric zip pull cut from a school scarf. Eileen has a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek, with short white hair and darker eyebrows. Eileen holds eye contact until the other person has finished during a conversation.
personality: Eileen enjoys routines and will defend the right of someone else to break one. As a result, Eileen is often everyone's favorite cover for a missed morning.
agenda: To identify the stripe maker from the old factory.
family: Melanie Breen is Eileen’s cousin’s child. Eileen is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Melanie calls about good news first. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *A borrowed name*, Melanie says, “My own name was changed at immigration. I lent the writer the two spellings I live under.”
connections: Gabriel Han. The fabric worker helps distinguish two umbrellas before anyone walks home in rain.

reactions.situation: Both umbrella owners turn up at the beach
reactions.response: Eileen gets the two families together in the shade to identify the items.

reactions.situation: A family supper turns into an argument about old debt
reactions.response: Eileen asks each person to say what they believe is actually owed before anybody proposes a payment.

reactions.situation: If a family plan changes at the door
reactions.response: Eileen keeps a place for the late person without making the others postpone their meal.
